title: The Hazelnut Block Pietro Ferrero Made When Cocoa Ran Short
conflicts: Year-end 1946 production is given as 'over a thousand' without a unit (quintals or kilograms), so the story uses only the February figure (three quintals) and staff numbers, on which the company history and AGI agree. AFP's two obituary versions say hazelnut saved money on 'chocolate' or on 'cocoa'; the story says cocoa was scarce and dear, as the company and AGI do.
notes: AGI follows the company history closely in places, so AFP is used as the independent check on the substitution. The failed Turin shop is from AGI only and attributed. 'Bootstrapped' is an inference (no outside investors mentioned anywhere). The popular 'melted in a heatwave' origin tale was not used. Quote stance: affirms.
